text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key rule is to follow naming conventions: choose clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Keep functions small and focused on a single task, because short functions are easier to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, since fixing bugs or adding new features takes less time when the structure is simple. Remember that code is read far more often than it is written, so always write with the reader in mind.
